title: Mathematical definition proposals for synthetic testing

common_contract.input: Chronologically ordered, Data-Guard-validated archive rows with date and six-number draw; a separate ISO target_date.
common_contract.isolation: Only rows whose date is strictly earlier than target_date contribute numbers to any score. On/after-target number arrays must never be accessed.
common_contract.draw_constraints: Exactly six distinct integers in 1..60, internally sorted.
common_contract.ranking: Descending score, ascending number as stable tie-break.
common_contract.failures: Insufficient history returns no_signal and an empty candidate list; never fill with arbitrary numbers.
validation_protocols_after_approval: canonical archive integrity and target-isolation audit

proposals.source_relationship: Inspired by V8.6 transition signatures; deliberately repairs the legacy direction mismatch by using the historical C state as outcome.
mathematical_definition: Let pre-target history be D_0,...,D_m in chronological order, m>=2. The current observed transition is (A*,B*)=(D_(m-1),D_m).
For each historical triple i=0,...,m-2, define signature S_i=sign(Phi(D_i,D_(i+1))) and outcome C_i=D_(i+2). The current signature is S*=sign(Phi(A*,B*)).
Phi concatenates V8.6 features posdiff, gapdiff, parityflip, bandmove, mod3diff, mod5diff, mod7diff, sumdiff, span_diff, shape_diff and signed_core. rawdiff is omitted because it duplicates posdiff.
d_i is Hamming distance between S* and S_i. Sort examples by (d_i ascending, i descending), select at most the nearest five.
For rank r starting at 1, add 1/r to score(y) for every y in C_i of the selected example at rank r. Return positive-score numbers by score descending then number ascending.
proposals.insufficient_history: Fewer than three pre-target draws -> no_signal; no synthetic fallback values.
proposals.key_test: A repeating synthetic transition A->B whose observed continuation is C must rank C, not B.
proposals.legacy_mismatch: The legacy evaluator votes on B, so its results do not prove an A->B->C predictor.

proposals.source_relationship: Formalizes the old gen_pair_relation source-number to next-draw-number count, including its top-10-per-source behavior.
mathematical_definition: Let pre-target history be D_0,...,D_m; the latest source A*=D_m.
For every historical transition i=0,...,m-1, define M[x,y]=sum_i 1{x in D_i}*1{y in D_(i+1)} for x,y in 1..60.
For each x in A*, choose the up-to-ten y with M[x,y]>0 having highest M[x,y], ties by ascending y.
score(y)=sum over x in A* of M[x,y] when y belongs to that x's selected top-ten list; otherwise that source contributes zero.
Return positive-score numbers by score descending then number ascending.
proposals.insufficient_history: Fewer than 20 pre-target draws -> no_signal; no arbitrary filler numbers.
proposals.key_test: When the synthetic history repeatedly maps every current-source number to a known next state, that next state must receive the top scores.
proposals.legacy_mismatch: This is a descriptive co-occurrence candidate, not evidence of causation or predictive advantage.

proposals.source_relationship: A new explicit proposal, not the same as the legacy V8.6 mod5diff transition feature.

parameters.vote: unweighted presence per selected next draw

mathematical_definition: For each draw D define MOD5(D)=(c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4), where c_r is the number of n in D for which n mod 5=r.
For the latest pre-target source D_m, compute the L1 distance from MOD5(D_m) to each source profile MOD5(D_i) from fully historical transitions D_i->D_(i+1), i=0,...,m-1.
Sort transitions by (distance ascending, i descending) and keep at most five nearest transitions.
score(y)=the number of selected next-draw sets D_(i+1) that contain y. Return positive-score numbers by score descending then number ascending.
proposals.insufficient_history: Fewer than six pre-target draws -> no_signal; no arbitrary filler numbers.
proposals.key_test: For a residue-profile repeated in the synthetic history, the corresponding known next draw must rank highest.
proposals.legacy_mismatch: The old mod5diff is a per-position transition-change feature; it does not specify a mapping from a MOD5 state to T.
